title: HUMAN PREFERENCES IN LARGE LANGUAGE MODEL LATENT SPACE: A TECHNICAL ANALYSIS ON THE RELIABILITY OF SYNTHETIC DATA IN VOTING OUTCOME PREDICTION

bias_targets.methodology: Using trained linear probes to identify political party affiliations in the models' latent space and comparing the predicted voting distributions of base versus aligned models to real-world election survey data.
Calculating and comparing the normalized entropy of latent political voting predictions across various age subgroups against real-world human survey data.
Calculating and comparing the variance and normalized entropy of political voting predictions for male versus female personas against real-world baselines.
Measuring the latent space persona-to-party mappings and voting prediction entropy across personas with varying education backgrounds, household income levels, and employment statuses.
Analyzing the differences in latent political ascriptions and voting prediction entropy for personas residing in East versus West Germany.
